recognize_zh: 周邊血液抹片中央一個圓形小體含許多紫色點狀染色質，附在一個淡染、幾近空影的紅血球輪廓上，外觀提示間日瘧（Plasmodium vivax）的分裂體或破裂寄生蟲；但解析度有限，看不到色素與薛夫納氏小點（Schüffner dots），分期無法確定。
features: Compact round parasite-like body smaller than a red cell, containing numerous punctate purple chromatin dots
Associated pale, poorly hemoglobinized ghost-like host cell outline extending from the body
Malarial pigment and Schüffner stippling not clearly resolved at this magnification
Surrounding red cells normocytic without other parasitized cells in the field
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a compact round body, smaller than an adjacent red cell, containing numerous punctate purple chromatin dots and associated with a pale, ghost-like host cell outline. The appearance is suggestive of a Plasmodium schizont with multiple merozoites or a parasite released from a lysed red cell. Malarial pigment, Schüffner stippling and host cell enlargement cannot be confidently assessed, and no other parasitized cells are present in this field. Findings are suggestive of, but not by themselves diagnostic of, Plasmodium vivax infection; species confirmation requires review of additional parasite stages on thick and thin films or PCR.

ddx.vs: P. ovale also enlarges red cells with Schüffner dots but produces oval, fimbriated host cells and schizonts with fewer (about 8) merozoites.
Falciparum schizonts are rarely seen in peripheral blood, and the smear typically shows multiple delicate ring forms and banana-shaped gametocytes in normal-sized cells.

ddx.dx: Platelet clump or giant platelet overlying a red cell
ddx.vs: Platelets show granular purple centers without discrete chromatin dots or pigment and lack a surrounding parasitized host cell.
Babesia forms small pleomorphic rings and tetrads (Maltese cross) without schizonts or pigment.
